Full details: Title check

**Explanation** The title "fix(clients): unloaded thread links show their title and project icon" matches the main change. The changeset adds a metadata-only read (title and project ID) for thread links whose threads are missing from the loaded thread list, and the link chips now use that data for the title and project icon across the clients. The title is specific and follows conventional commit style. The title does not mention the legacy environment resolution or the server-side RPC, but those are supporting parts of the same fix.
Full details: Description check

**Explanation** The description follows the template's main sections. The Problem section explains the bug: existing threads showed "Thread no longer available" when their metadata was absent from the loaded list, and searching for the thread recovered the link. The Change section explains the metadata-only read, the fallbacks, and the older server behavior. The Verification section lists the checks run (vp run check:changed, browser navigation regressions, server and client runtime tests). The Scope and approval section is weak. It cites related issues (`#26467`, `#32541`) and overlapping PRs but does not link a triaged bug issue or a maintainer approval comment, and it does not explain why the change qualifies as a small focused fix without prior approval. The Verification section also does not include before/after screenshots for the UI change, and it does not state anything that could not be checked. The description is mostly complete, but the approval evidence is missing. **Resolution** Add a link to the triaged bug issue or to the maintainer approval comment in the Scope and approval section. If no prior approval exists, explain why this fix qualifies as a very small, focused fix of an obvious bug. Add before/after screenshots of the title and project icon for the UI change, or a short recording of the loading behavior. State anything that was not checked.

`99-101`: ** Trivial** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Wait for navigation before asserting the router location.** The test reads `screen.router?.state.location.pathname` right after `await link.click()`. Router navigation is asynchronous. The assertion can run before the location updates, which makes the test flaky. Wrap each location check in `vi.waitFor`. Alternatively, assert through `expect.element`.
Proposed fix for the first assertion

```diff - expect(screen.router?.state.location.pathname).toBe( - `/environment/${encodeURIComponent(threadId)}`, - ); + await vi.waitFor(() => + expect(screen.router?.state.location.pathname).toBe( + `/environment/${encodeURIComponent(threadId)}`, + ), + ); ```
Apply the same change at Lines 114 and 121. As per path instructions: "Hold changed tests to the rules in docs/internals/testing.md." The rules require that "Browser tests assert through `expect.element` or `vi.waitFor`". Also applies to: 114-114, 121-121
